lesson.title: The Return That Shrinks Serve +1
lesson.hook: You chase the open corner, miss returns, and let the server start every pattern comfortably.
lesson.tomorrow: Next time a server controls serve-plus-one, test depth through the middle.

pro.label: De Minaur's return, 2024
pro.moment: Against first serves, de Minaur sent 55% of his returns down the middle third of the court.
pro.read: An unglamorous target can take their weapon away.

drill.name: Middle and deep
drill.how: Returns score only if they land in the middle third of the court and past the service line. The server plays the point out.

steps.name: Pulled wide by a first serve
steps.sit: A big first serve pulls you wide. The server stays back for their next ball.
opts: Hard and deep to the far sideline
steps.payoff: Deep through the middle keeps the server back and takes away their angle.
steps.principle: When the serve stretches you, take away their options before looking for space.
steps.why: Through the middle has the most margin and leaves them no easy angle. It won't stop every attack, but it stops the easy one.
steps.take: Pulled wide by a big serve? Block it deep through the middle.

lines.A: From out wide, the far sideline asks too much — wide.
lines.B: Deep through the middle keeps them back — stretched, but still in it.
lines.C: Short through the middle — they step in and attack.
lines.D: Short crosscourt — they step in; you can't get back.

steps.name: Short middle, deep middle
steps.sit: Two returns through the middle. One lands near the service line; one lands deep.
steps.q: What makes the difference to the server?
opts: The middle takes away their reach
The short one makes them move more
The pace matters more than the landing
The deep one keeps them back
steps.payoff: The short one let them hit from inside the court.
steps.principle: Through the middle isn't enough on its own. It has to be deep.
steps.why: Both returns cleared the sidelines. Watch where the server hits each one: inside the court on the short one, behind the baseline on the deep one.
steps.take: Through the middle isn't enough — it has to land deep.

lines.A: Both went through the middle — the difference is where they met it.
lines.B: The short one made them move less — they stepped straight in.
lines.C: The landing did the work, not the pace.
lines.D: Right — the short one they meet inside the court; the deep one keeps them back.

steps.ph: Transfer · Let the serve change the job
steps.name: Softer second serve
steps.sit: Now a soft second serve sits up. You're early, and the server has drifted left.
steps.q: What does this serve let you do?
opts: Block it through the middle again
Into the open half, well inside
steps.payoff: Time and balance: now you can attack the open half.
steps.principle: Block when you're stretched. Attack when the serve gives you time.
steps.why: The soft serve gave you time, and the server is off to one side. Use the space, but aim well inside the lines: the line adds risk you don't need.
steps.take: Soft second serve, server off to one side? Attack the space, with margin.

lines.A: Safe, but the rally just starts again — the chance goes.
lines.B: Short toward them — they step in and attack.
lines.C: Into the open half, well inside the lines — too far for them.
lines.D: Hard at the line from inside — a fraction long.
